title: ERP/SAP Consultant Roadmap
summary: Build IT and database fundamentals first, then learn business processes, SAP modules, configuration, integration, analytics and client-facing implementation skills.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and ending around 2030. The roadmap assumes a technical SAP consulting route; semester milestones can be shifted to match the university calendar.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Programming, SQL, databases, business-process modelling, ERP concepts, SAP fundamentals and internship/project experience.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: One SAP functional or technical lane, such as S/4HANA Finance, MM, SD, SuccessFactors, ABAP, Basis, integration or analytics.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Solution design, SAP implementation leadership, integration, data migration, architecture and client ownership.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Enterprise transformation, SAP architecture, cloud ERP, AI-enabled business processes, governance and strategic advisory.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If you choose the four-year honours/research variant, use the additional year for enterprise architecture, SAP integration, data/AI, ERP research, a substantial implementation project or an industry-sponsored capstone.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Do not remain limited to configuration in one module. Add integration, cloud ERP, data migration, security, automation and AI-enabled enterprise processes. The long-term progression is from module expertise toward solution architecture and transformation leadership.

PhD routes

Move from module-level consulting toward end-to-end enterprise transformation. Maintain technical depth in SAP architecture, integration, data and cloud while developing stronger knowledge of business strategy, governance, security and industry processes.
